question: A nurse accidentally drops and breaks an old mercury blood pressure machine on the ward floor. What kind of hazard is this?

options.A: Chemical hazard
options.B: Biological hazard
options.C: Genotoxic hazard
options.D: Radioactive hazard

explanation: Mercury is a toxic heavy metal, making it a chemical hazard. Its vapors can easily be breathed in or absorbed through the skin if not cleaned up properly! [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h3)

question: What are two major health risks associated with early unprotected sexual intercourse in adolescents?

options.A: Sexually transmitted infections and unintended pregnancies
options.B: Chronic respiratory illness and severe joint pain
options.C: Nutritional deficiencies and bone density loss
options.D: Visual impairment and cardiovascular disease

explanation: Unprotected sexual contact exposes young people directly to pathogens causing infections and fails to prevent fertilization, leading to high rates of teenage pregnancy. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the standard temperature range for maintaining the cold chain in vaccine storage?

options.A: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius
options.B: Plus 2 degrees Celsius to plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.C: Plus 37 degrees Celsius to plus 40 degrees Celsius
options.D: Minus 20 degrees Celsius to minus 10 degrees Celsius

explanation: Most standard vaccines must be kept refrigerated between +2°C and +8°C to prevent them from spoiling. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is a direct surveillance responsibility for a clinical nurse?

options.A: Enforcing federal health policies in the national parliament
options.B: Importing international vaccines for national distribution
options.C: Conducting post-mortem examinations on all deceased patients
options.D: Reporting suspected cases of priority diseases immediately

explanation: Nurses must promptly notify public health authorities when they encounter suspected cases of dangerous or reportable diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: What is the main job of bicarbonate in pancreatic juice?

options.A: Neutralizing the acidic chyme coming from the stomach
options.B: Breaking down large fat droplets into tiny pieces
options.C: Activating pepsinogen to start protein digestion
options.D: Lubricating the walls of the small intestine

explanation: Bicarbonate is basic (alkaline), so it acts like a peacekeeper, cooling down the harsh stomach acid as food enters the small intestine. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the best nursing action for a patient who cannot safely swallow food by mouth?

options.A: Forcing the patient to finish meals to maintain weight
options.B: Waiting until the patient asks for intravenous fluids
options.C: Stopping all fluid and medication administration
options.D: Managing alternative feeding methods like enteral tubes

explanation: You got it! When swallowing is unsafe, nurses step in to manage alternative routes—like a nasogastric (NG) tube—to keep the patient nourished safely. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h8)

question: How is a middle-range theory different from a grand nursing theory?

options.A: It is completely unproven and used only by student researchers
options.B: It applies strictly to hospital administration rather than patient care
options.C: It avoids using any concepts related to human behavior
options.D: It focuses on specific, manageable clinical situations rather than broad, universal ideas

explanation: Exactly. While grand theories try to explain all of nursing, middle-range theories zoom in on specific, everyday clinical situations that are easier to study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which neurotransmitter works to calm down electrical activity in the brain and balance things out?

options.A: GABA
options.B: Glutamate
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: GABA is the brain's main 'braking' system. It helps calm down nerve activity so things don't get too excited. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h5)

question: Which structure is known as the natural pacemaker of the heart?

options.A: Sinoatrial node
options.B: Bundle of His
options.C: Purkinje fibers
options.D: Atrioventricular node

explanation: The sinoatrial node sets the normal pace for the heart because it depolarizes faster than any other conducting tissue. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the name of the mature, fluid-filled follicle ready for release?

options.A: Primordial follicle
options.B: Corpus albicans
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, large, fluid-filled stage of follicular development that ruptures during ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h2)

question: When moving an injured person, what is the most important goal to keep in mind?

options.A: Reaching the nearest hospital in the shortest possible time
options.B: Ensuring the patient's family members can ride along
options.C: Clearing the emergency scene before law enforcement arrives
options.D: Moving the patient safely without causing further injury

explanation: You've got this! Safety and protecting the patient from extra harm always come first, even before rushing to the hospital. Great nursing instincts! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h1)

question: You just collected a wound swab from a patient with a leg ulcer. What's the best immediate step?

options.A: Place the swab inside a house refrigerator overnight to keep it cool
options.B: Send the specimen to the laboratory immediately in a proper transport container
options.C: Wash the cotton tip under running tap water to remove excess blood
options.D: Leave the capped tube on the nurse station desk until the end of the shift

explanation: Time is precious! Sending the sample straight away keeps fragile germs alive and stops normal skin bacteria from taking over. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is a big perk of having a 'flat' organizational structure in a hospital ward?

options.A: Orders take longer to reach the bedside staff
options.B: It completely removes the need for a head nurse
options.C: It creates more promotion posts for middle managers
options.D: Staff nurses can communicate more directly with top leadership

explanation: Spot on! By cutting out excess middle management, the distance between the bedside nurse and upper management shrinks, making communication much faster. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why is eating a balanced diet so important for women during their reproductive years?

options.A: It prepares the body for potential pregnancy and protects long-term health
options.B: It guarantees an increase in overall daily muscle mass
options.C: It eliminates the need for any future dietary supplements
options.D: It completely stops the symptoms of premenstrual syndrome

explanation: Great thinking! Keeping good nutrient stores ready helps support a healthy body now and protects both mom and baby if pregnancy happens down the line. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h1)

question: An adult child is crying and demanding that staff restart all life support for a dying parent, even though the parent has a clear living will stating otherwise. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Act as an advocate for the patient by gently reminding the family of the documented wishes
options.B: Tell the family that their opinion does not matter at all in the hospital
options.C: Immediately follow the child's orders to stop the family conflict
options.D: Call hospital security to remove the family member from the room

explanation: The nurse bridges the gap with compassion, offering emotional support while firmly upholding the documented autonomy of the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why must nurse managers actively supervise instead of just writing policies on paper?

options.A: Written policies alone cannot guarantee staff will follow them safely
options.B: Nurse managers have no other administrative duties assigned to them
options.C: Staff nurses prefer having constant supervision during every shift
options.D: Hospital accreditation bodies legally require daily verbal check-ins

explanation: Having a policy on paper is a good start, but checking actual practice ensures everyone is safe and rules are followed in real clinical situations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h1)

question: A mother wants to mark her newborn baby for protection. How should the nurse best handle this counseling?

options.A: Threaten to call security if she attempts the procedure
options.B: Perform the cuts safely using hospital surgical blades
options.C: Explain infection risks gently and suggest safer alternatives
options.D: Ignore the conversation because it is a private family matter

explanation: That's brilliant nursing! Respectful education bridges cultural beliefs with health safety without pushing the client away. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h6)

question: Which of these is a common cause of an inaccurate glucometer reading?

options.A: Using too little blood on the test strip
options.B: Pricking the side of the finger
options.C: Wiping the outside of the meter clean
options.D: Checking blood sugar before breakfast

explanation: The strip needs enough blood to fill the reaction zone. If the sample is too small, the meter might give an error or a false reading. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why would a doctor choose a nasal endoscope instead of a basic speculum exam?

options.A: To stop sudden nosebleeds in the front septum
options.B: To measure air pressure inside the cheek sinuses
options.C: To test the patient's sense of smell
options.D: To look deep inside the nasal passages and sinus openings

explanation: Nasal endoscopes use tiny cameras and lights to see past the front of the nose into deeper areas a regular speculum can't reach. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why do teenagers often take big risks even when they know it's dangerous?

options.A: They experience a permanent loss of short-term memory
options.B: They completely lack the ability to think logically
options.C: Their cognitive development stops entirely during puberty
options.D: Reward-seeking brain centers develop faster than impulse-control centers

explanation: The thrill-seeking part of the brain develops faster than the brake pedal (impulse control), making exciting experiences feel totally worth the risk to them. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the main reason nurses get professional malpractice insurance?

options.A: To cover personal medical bills during a workplace illness
options.B: To guarantee a higher salary within hospital settings
options.C: To replace the need for an active nursing license renewal
options.D: To provide financial protection against legal claims of professional negligence

explanation: Malpractice insurance is there to protect you from the huge financial stress of lawsuits if a mistake or negligence is claimed. You've got this! [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which question is a patient in the anger stage most likely to ask?

options.A: How much will this treatment cost?
options.B: When will my test results arrive?
options.C: Can we negotiate more time?
options.D: Why is this happening to me?

explanation: Anger comes from deep hurt and the feeling of unfairness, making patients ask 'Why me?' [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important to talk about pain management before the patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Pain medications must be taken to prevent allergic reactions to the drug
options.B: Analgesics speed up the absorption of the hormone in the stomach lining
options.C: Misoprostol causes strong uterine contractions that lead to significant cramping
options.D: Pain medication stops the excessive bleeding that occurs right away

explanation: Cramping is a very normal part of the process because the uterus is working hard to empty. Planning ahead for pain relief keeps our patients comfortable! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h4)

question: Which germ is the main cause of Tuberculosis (TB)?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation: You've got this! TB is caused by a tough germ called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Knowing your causative agents is key on the wards! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the main difference between Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State (HHS) and Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?

options.A: The presence of severe hypoglycemia in HHS
options.B: The absence of significant ketoacidosis in HHS
options.C: The rapid onset of kidney failure in DKA
options.D: The lack of dehydration in DKA

explanation: HHS usually happens in Type 2 diabetes where there is still just enough insulin around to stop major fat breakdown, so ketones don't build up like they do in DKA. Great clinical distinction to master! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing hereditary conditions?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to speak directly with patients
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members for every patient
options.C: No single profession has all the skills needed to address complex genetic and social needs
options.D: It ensures that laboratory scientists make all final clinical decisions

explanation: Hereditary conditions involve medical, emotional, and social challenges that require diverse expertise from multiple healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why do doctors order cardiac enzyme blood tests for a patient with severe chest pain?

options.A: To measure how fast red blood cells are moving
options.B: To test the liver's ability to process fats
options.C: To find out if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if heart muscle tissue has been injured

explanation: When heart cells die from lack of oxygen, they release specific enzymes into the bloodstream, confirming a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h5)

question: A community nurse visits a patient with psychosis who looks very suspicious and guarded. What is the best first move?

options.A: Start with calm, non-threatening social conversation before asking clinical questions
options.B: Confront the client about their false beliefs right away to establish reality
options.C: Immediately demand a urine sample to check for illicit drug use
options.D: Leave the home immediately without assessing to avoid agitation

explanation: Brilliant! Taking it slow and building a friendly rapport helps lower anxiety so the patient feels safe enough to talk. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T3#GNS324_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why should health education messages in primary care be tailored to the local culture?

options.A: It reduces the cost of printing textbooks
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical treatment protocols
options.C: It ensures the community understands and easily relates to the information
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to speak in English

explanation: Using familiar language, cultural examples, and local methods makes health teaching more acceptable and effective. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why is an unsafe injection a big deal in public health?

options.A: It almost always leads to immediate surgical site infections
options.B: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who receives it
options.C: It can easily transmit serious bloodborne infections to healthy individuals
options.D: It guarantees that the administered drug will not work properly

explanation: Unsafe practices bypass the skin's natural defenses, which can directly spread heavy infections like HIV and hepatitis into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a retrospective research study?

options.A: Testing a new drug in real time
options.B: Examining past events and records
options.C: Observing an active clinical trial
options.D: Following healthy patients for years

explanation: Great job! Think of 'retrospective' like looking in a rearview mirror—these studies look backward at data or events that already happened instead of following people forward. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T14#GNS224_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why do many lung cancer patients only discover they are sick when the disease is already advanced?

options.A: The lungs lack pain receptors, allowing tumors to grow undetected initially.
options.B: Symptoms only appear after the cancer completely destroys the heart.
options.C: Early lung tumors cause immediate total paralysis of the limbs.
options.D: Blood tests detect the cancer cells only during late stages.

explanation: You got it! Because lung tissue doesn't have pain nerve endings, a small tumor can grow quietly for a long time without causing any physical pain. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a danger sign that requires immediate emergency referral during pregnancy?

options.A: Severe, throbbing headache with blurred vision
options.B: Sudden gush or trickle of fluid from the vagina before term
options.C: Mild, occasional dependent ankle swelling at the end of the day
options.D: Bright red vaginal bleeding at any gestational age

explanation: Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day is super common due to extra pressure in the lower body. But bleeding, sudden fluid leakage, and bad headaches are red flags! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h5)

question: A patient refuses malaria treatment because they feel the drugs are too expensive and far away. In the Health Belief Model, what is this called?

options.A: Perceived severity
options.B: Perceived barriers
options.C: Perceived benefits
options.D: Perceived susceptibility

explanation: Perceived barriers are the hurdles, costs, or inconveniences that make someone hesitant to take healthy actions. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why should you as a nurse encourage older patients to do tasks themselves instead of doing everything for them?

options.A: To reduce the total number of nursing staff needed on duty
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge paperwork process
options.C: To comply with strict hospital punishment regulations
options.D: To prevent rapid physical deconditioning and loss of ability

explanation: Spot on! When older adults stop moving and doing things, their muscles weaken very fast. Encouraging self-care keeps them strong and mobile. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a negative feedback loop in the body?

options.A: To trigger rapid nerve impulses during acute physical pain
options.B: To maintain hormone levels within a stable, normal range
options.C: To continuously amplify hormone production until exhaustion
options.D: To replace lost nutrients in the extracellular fluid

explanation: Think of negative feedback like an air conditioner: when the room gets too cold (or hormone levels get too high), it turns things off to keep balance. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T4#GNS211_U1_T4_h5)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fever after drinking fresh, unpasteurized milk from a family farm. What is the most likely source of infection?

options.A: An infected livestock animal
options.B: A contaminated surgical instrument
options.C: An asymptomatic human carrier
options.D: Stagnant hospital tap water

explanation: Unpasteurized dairy is a classic route for catching zoonotic bugs straight from farm animals like cows or goats. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h3)

question: What is the most immediate, life-threatening danger for a mother with a placental abnormality?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Urinary tract infection

explanation: When the placenta doesn't attach or separate normally, the womb often struggles to clamp down afterward, leading to heavy, dangerous bleeding. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why must patients take off all jewelry and metal objects before a CT scan?

options.A: Metal attracts the magnetic radiation from the machine
options.B: Metal heats up dangerously during the scan process
options.C: Metal objects cause artifact streaks on the images
options.D: Metal interferes with the hospital Wi-Fi signals

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely and creates ugly, bright streaks on the scan that can hide important details. Always good to remember in clinicals! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T13#GNS123_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the term for the severe muscle wasting and extreme weight loss seen in many advanced cancer patients?

options.A: Metaplasia
options.B: Polycythemia
options.C: Cachexia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Cancer cachexia is a tough syndrome where the body rapidly wastes away its muscle and fat, despite eating. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why do healthcare providers often use the umbilical vein for emergency drugs in the delivery room?

options.A: It provides fast, reliable access to the central circulation
options.B: It avoids the risk of fluid infiltration into tissues
options.C: It prevents the need for any sterile preparation
options.D: It allows continuous blood pressure monitoring only

explanation: The umbilical vein is wide, easy to find in an emergency, and leads straight to the main bloodstream, getting life-saving drugs where they need to go fast. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h6)

question: What type of tissue makes up uterine fibroids?

options.A: Malignant epithelial tissue
options.B: Infected lymphatic fluid
options.C: Hardened calcified bone
options.D: Benign smooth muscle cells

explanation: Correct! Fibroids (also called leiomyomas) are simply non-cancerous growths made of the uterus's own smooth muscle cells. Nothing to panic about! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h2)

question: Which finding around a skeletal traction pin site should you report as a sign of infection?

options.A: Purulent drainage and foul odor
options.B: Dry crusting around the metal insertion point
options.C: Mild pinkness that fades within the first day
options.D: Small amounts of clear serosanguinous drainage

explanation: You got it! Pus and bad smells are telltale signs of bacteria at work. Light pinkness or dry crusting can just be normal early healing. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h4)

question: You are about to give an oral med, but you notice the patient's ID band doesn't match the chart. What should you do FIRST?

options.A: Leave the medication at the bedside table for the patient to take later
options.B: Withhold the medication and verify patient identity using the chart and verbal inquiry
options.C: Ask another student nurse to give the medication instead
options.D: Administer the medication anyway since you know the patient's face

explanation: Safety first! Never guess or skip ID checks. Always pause, withhold the drug, and sort out the correct identity before proceeding. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the biggest downside or risk linked to the intraperitoneal route?

options.A: High risk of infection and peritonitis
options.B: Complete failure of the human respiratory system
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Instantaneous destruction of all oral medications

explanation: You got it! Anytime you open up or access the sterile peritoneal cavity, germs can sneak in, making infection and peritonitis the main danger to watch for. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h7)

question: A client is discharged after an abortion without a birth control method and fails to return for her two-week checkup. What major risk does she face?

options.A: A permanent inability to ever produce estrogen again
options.B: An unintended repeat pregnancy due to early ovulation
options.C: Severe weight loss from sudden hormonal withdrawal
options.D: An automatic infection in the uterine lining

explanation: Missing the follow-up without a started method leaves a gap in protection during a time when fertility has already returned. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: What do social systems like schools and local clinics do for a community?

options.A: They prevent all members from ever experiencing chronic illnesses
options.B: They replace the need for individual family support structures
options.C: They dictate the exact weather patterns and agricultural seasons
options.D: They provide the organized institutions needed to meet basic human needs

explanation: Exactly! Social systems are like the pillars of a society—hospitals, schools, and markets work together to keep everyday life running smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T1#GNS225_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the core philosophy of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Bringing essential health services as close as possible to where people live
options.B: Focusing treatment exclusively on patients who can pay cash
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign medical aid for community survival
options.D: Building high-tech specialist hospitals in major metropolitan cities

explanation: PHC emphasizes grassroots accessibility, making basic health promotion and disease prevention available to everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is high reliability so important for our nursing research tools?

options.A: It proves the researchers spent enough money on equipment
options.B: It ensures study results are free from random measurement errors
options.C: It guarantees that patients will recover faster on the ward
options.D: It stops patients from dropping out of clinical trials early

explanation: Reliable tools cut out the guesswork and random noise. When we use them, we can trust our data reflects what's truly happening on the ward! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h1)

question: Which life process helps the body sense changes around it and react?

options.A: Differentiation
options.B: Excretion
options.C: Reproduction
options.D: Responsiveness

explanation: Responsiveness is your body's alert system! It's how you detect things like heat, cold, or pain and react quickly to stay safe. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the core message of the contingency approach to management?

options.A: Every hospital must use the exact same leadership rules
options.B: Financial incentives are the only way to motivate staff
options.C: Managers should never change their personal leadership style
options.D: The best management style depends on the specific situation

explanation: Contingency theory teaches that leaders must adapt their approach based on the unique demands of each scenario. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which type of larvae is mainly responsible for causing myiasis (infestation of tissue) in humans?

options.A: Moth caterpillars
options.B: Dipterous fly larvae
options.C: Aquatic mosquito larvae
options.D: Seed tick arachnids

explanation: Flies from the Diptera order lay eggs that hatch into maggots, which can feed on human tissue and cause myiasis. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which service is typically offered by community groups like adult day care centers?

options.A: Respite and temporary relief for family caregivers
options.B: Inpatient surgical procedures for chronic conditions
options.C: Emergency ambulance transport during a stroke
options.D: Permanent residential nursing home placement

explanation: Adult day care centers provide a safe, fun space for older adults during the day, giving family caregivers a well-deserved break to rest or work. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of family dysfunction or distress?

options.A: Young children forced into premature caregiving roles
options.B: Open, respectful communication and shared problem-solving
options.C: Unresolved domestic violence and persistent household conflict
options.D: Severe social isolation from neighbors

explanation: Open communication and teamwork are signs of a healthy, happy family, not a dysfunctional one! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is knowing the route of transmission important for a nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for hand hygiene in clean wards
options.B: It predicts the exact day the patient will be discharged
options.C: It determines which antibiotic the doctor will prescribe first
options.D: It helps choose the correct isolation and barrier precautions

explanation: When nurses know how a germ travels, they can block that path using masks, gloves, or specific room placements. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: Why do nurses place an unconscious, breathing patient into the lateral recovery position?

options.A: To stop the patient from experiencing painful muscle spasms
options.B: To prevent the tongue from blocking the airway and reduce the risk of aspiration
options.C: To increase blood flow directly to the frontal lobes of the cerebrum
options.D: To make it easier for nurses to check blood pressure every hour

explanation: Great thinking! Gravity helps pull saliva or vomit away from the airway when they lie safely on their side. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the main limitation of using a 24-hour dietary recall?

options.A: It relies heavily on the patient's memory and may not show normal eating habits
options.B: It is too expensive for routine use in busy outpatient clinics
options.C: It requires the patient to write down every meal for an entire month
options.D: It only measures fluid intake and ignores solid foods entirely

explanation: A single day may represent an unusual eating day, such as a holiday or a day of illness, and patients often forget items they consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h4)

question: Why can blocking dopamine in the tuberoinfundibular pathway lead to higher prolactin levels?

options.A: Prolactin is converted into dopamine in the bloodstream
options.B: Dopamine directly stimulates the pituitary gland to produce milk
options.C: Blockade destroys the cells that store prolactin
options.D: Dopamine normally acts to inhibit prolactin release

explanation: Normally, dopamine acts like a brake on prolactin. When antipsychotics block that dopamine, you take the brake off, and prolactin levels rise. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h2)

question: Why do healthcare planners conduct a community needs assessment before setting up PAC services?

options.A: To recruit international doctors for specialized surgeries
options.B: To penalize traditional healers practicing in the village
options.C: To understand local barriers, health data, and access challenges
options.D: To determine the exact cost of medical equipment imports

explanation: A needs assessment helps us see what real-life factors delay care in the community—like transport issues or cultural fears—so we can design services that truly help people. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h2)

question: Why might a patient with acute leukemia have swollen, bleeding gums?

question: Which of the following is a normal age-related change in the cardiovascular system?

question: Why do we use a tiered, step-by-step system for healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

question: Which of these is a basic shared need that brings a community together?

question: Why is it important to test blood sugar while a patient is fasting?

question: Which human infectious disease is the only one successfully eradicated globally so far?

question: What happens when a germ changes its target binding site?

question: Why is it important for nurses to talk and debrief with colleagues after a patient's traumatic death?

question: What is the main chemical messenger targeted by NK1 receptor blockers like aprepitant?

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

question: An abnormal hole between the two lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart is known as:

question: Which physical sign is a classic warning flag that a patient might be experiencing abuse?

question: What is the main advantage of using the IMCI strategy when treating sick children?

question: What is the primary goal of teaching communities about infection control?

question: What is the main goal of epidemiology in public health?

question: What is an important nursing check after a patient has an upper GI scope (endoscopy)?

question: Why must a nurse use soap and water instead of alcohol gel after caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile?

question: A patient arrives from a terrible car crash with massive internal bleeding. What must the trauma suite have ready immediately?

question: Which of these is a key part of healthy sleep hygiene?

question: What is a major cause of unsafe injection risks in informal healthcare settings?

question: A patient asks why they got an autoimmune disease while their sibling living in the same house did not. What best explains this?

question: An 8-month-old baby is brought in with a cough and fast breathing. What sign tells you the baby needs antibiotics for pneumonia?

question: What is a very common emotional reaction for someone dealing with new or worsening hearing loss?

question: What is a common clinical consequence for nurses when the health sector is chronically underfunded?

question: Why does lacking thiamine cause brain cells to die so quickly?

options.C: A temporary change in her favorite foods
options.D: Mild fatigue and slight spotting for two days

question: What is the main job of emergency contraception?

options.A: To terminate an established pregnancy safely
options.B: To serve as a regular daily family planning method
options.C: To prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse
options.D: To protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Think of emergency contraception as your backup plan after a contraceptive slip-up or unprotected sex. It is not meant for daily family planning and doesn't work if a pregnancy has already started. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just brush off sudden confusion in an older patient as 'normal aging'?

options.A: It violates hospital discharge policies for elderly patients
options.B: It can cause the nurse to miss a treatable underlying medical problem
options.C: It always leads to immediate legal action from family members
options.D: It speeds up the natural physical decline of the brain

explanation: Never assume confusion is just old age! Sudden changes in mental status can be signs of something serious and treatable, like an infection, stroke, or delirium. Always investigate further. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the best way to assess a toddler's neurological function during a physical exam?

options.A: Observe their spontaneous play and developmental milestones
options.B: Ask them to complete a written multiple-choice test
options.C: Keep them completely still and silent for thirty minutes
options.D: Perform a strict formal cranial nerve exam immediately

explanation: Toddlers cannot follow complex commands, so observing natural movement and play provides the best clinical insight. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h7)

question: What happens to a patient's taste buds after a few weeks of following a low salt diet?

options.A: They gradually adjust, making foods taste flavorful with less salt
options.B: They permanently lose the ability to taste warm foods
options.C: They demand twice as much salt to feel any satisfaction
options.D: They become completely numb to all sweet and bitter tastes

explanation: Taste buds adapt over time, meaning food that initially tastes bland will eventually become satisfying as the palate resets. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h7)

question: What are the core parts of comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Antibiotic therapy alone without any further clinical follow-up
options.B: Criminal investigation, legal counseling, and mandatory detention
options.C: Surgical sterilization, blood transfusions, and long-term isolation
options.D: Emergency treatment, family planning, and reproductive health linkages

explanation: Wonderful! PAC is a complete package that covers acute medical treatment, birth control counseling, and connection to wider health resources. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h5)

question: What is the main job of insulin at the cellular level?

options.A: It converts dietary protein directly into red blood cells
options.B: It signals the kidneys to absorb more sugar into the bloodstream
options.C: It destroys excess bacteria circulating in the plasma
options.D: It acts as a key to unlock cell receptors and let glucose inside

explanation: You can picture insulin as a tiny key. It unlocks the doors of our body cells so glucose from the food we eat can go inside and give us energy. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h2)

question: How does chronic cervicitis mainly differ from acute cervicitis?

options.A: It involves long-standing immune cell changes in the tissue.
options.B: It presents with sudden, severe pus-like discharge.
options.C: It never requires any medical or nursing intervention.
options.D: It is always caused by viral agents rather than bacteria.

explanation: Think of acute as sudden and angry with quick pus, while chronic is a longer-lasting, low-grade immune response in the tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: What is the main goal of doing a health assessment right inside a patient's home?

options.A: To enforce strict hospital rules in a private residential property
options.B: To evaluate how well a person manages their health in their daily living space
options.C: To replace the need for routine visits to the primary doctor
options.D: To test family members on basic nursing and medical procedures

explanation: Spot on! Home assessments help us see how patients truly cope with their health right where they live every day. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h1)

question: Who has the main responsibility for setting health rules that must be followed in a school?

options.A: The local police department
options.B: Enrolling students
options.C: Parent-teacher athletics committees
options.D: School management

explanation: Exactly! The school management team holds the authority required to create and enforce official health policies. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of chief cells in the stomach?

options.A: Secreting pepsinogen for protein digestion
options.B: Releasing gastrin into the bloodstream
options.C: Producing a protective bicarbonate layer
options.D: Absorbing digested water and alcohol

explanation: You got it! Chief cells release pepsinogen, which stomach acid turns into pepsin to help break down the proteins you eat. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which side effect is very common with progestin-only injectable contraceptives (like Depo-Provera)?

options.A: Permanent complete hair loss
options.B: Changes in menstrual bleeding patterns
options.C: Sudden swelling of the thyroid gland
options.D: Instant weight loss of 20kg

explanation: Correct! Injectables often change how periods look—some spotting, heavier days, or periods stopping completely are quite normal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h6)

question: How can nurse leaders best help staff accept new policies suggested by an audit?

options.A: By threatening immediate dismissal for anyone who asks questions
options.B: By doubling the workload without increasing lunch break times
options.C: By keeping all audit findings completely secret from bedside nurses
options.D: By explaining the reasons behind the changes and involving them early

explanation: Involving frontline nurses and explaining the 'why' builds massive trust. When staff understand the goal, they embrace new policies so much better! [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h7)

question: Which teaching style works best when you are educating a patient who was just diagnosed with diabetes?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on severe complications like kidney failure
options.B: Tailoring information to fit the patient's daily routine and lifestyle
options.C: Insisting that they completely change their diet in one single day
options.D: Handing them a complex medical textbook to read overnight

explanation: Teaching works best when it's practical, personalized, and fits smoothly into the patient's real everyday life. Fantastic work finishing this set! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h8)

question: What is the main reason we use the cold chain system in healthcare?

options.A: To store expired drugs safely until disposal
options.B: To freeze all liquid medications before use
options.C: To speed up the delivery of emergency medicines
options.D: To keep vaccines within a safe temperature range

explanation: Think of the cold chain as an unbroken temperature bridge. It protects vaccines from factory to patient so they don't spoil. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h1)

question: How can you make sure your patient truly understands a new reproductive medication?

options.A: By assuming the pharmacist already covered everything needed
options.B: By handing the patient a technical textbook to read alone
options.C: By focusing only on how much the prescription costs
options.D: By explaining expected benefits, side effects, and warning signs clearly

explanation: Exactly! Taking time to explain how the drug works and what side effects to watch for helps your patient stay safe and confident. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why should you schedule planned rest breaks for a hospitalized patient with severe anaemia?

options.A: To lower blood pressure before giving medications
options.B: To give the digestive tract time to process iron pills
options.C: To prevent blood clots from forming in the legs
options.D: To reduce the overall oxygen demand on the body

explanation: Resting lowers the body's workload, which saves precious oxygen for a patient who tires out easily. Pacing is key in nursing care! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is a major reason farm crops get wasted before they ever reach the market?

options.A: Excessive consumer demand in local supermarkets
options.B: Poor storage facilities and inadequate transport networks
options.C: Immediate consumption of all crops by farmers
options.D: Strict government laws against selling fresh crops

explanation: Bad roads and lack of proper storage silos mean harvested food often spoils before getting to people who need it. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T027#GNS227_U2_T027_h2)

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer comes in with a swollen right leg and dull flank pain. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Metastatic spread of cancer cells to the bones of the foot
options.B: Tumor compression of pelvic veins and the ureter
options.C: Development of deep vein thrombosis from excessive physical activity
options.D: Severe systemic dehydration caused by heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Makes sense when you picture it: a growing tumor in the pelvis can press against nearby blood vessels (causing leg swelling) and block the tubes leading from the kidneys, known as the ureters (causing flank pain). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing an accurate baseline assessment upon ICU admission?

options.A: To provide a reference point for detecting future changes
options.B: To determine the exact discharge date
options.C: To eliminate the need for future vital sign checks
options.D: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements

explanation: You cannot spot an abnormal change if you do not know what the patient's normal starting point looked like when they arrived. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of teamwork between doctors, nurses, and dietitians in clinical nutrition?

options.A: Ensuring that the doctor makes all decisions without team input
options.B: Eliminating the need for nursing documentation on patient wards
options.C: Preventing gaps in care through shared expertise and communication
options.D: Reducing the number of working hours required for hospital staff

explanation: You got it! When healthcare professionals share their skills and communicate openly, patient care becomes much safer and more effective. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h7)

question: What is the biggest risk when a country relies heavily on foreign donor funding for healthcare?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take modern medications
options.B: The government will collect too much tax revenue locally
options.C: Programs may collapse if donor priorities or foreign policies change
options.D: Hospitals will automatically stop accepting local currency

explanation: Foreign aid can be unpredictable. If donors suddenly change their minds or pack up and leave, local health programs can fall apart if there's no backup plan. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h5)

question: How can an unusually long fallopian tube affect the movement of an egg?

options.A: It slows down movement and can trap the egg inside
options.B: It stops the uterus from making female hormones
options.C: It completely stops the ovary from releasing eggs
options.D: It speeds up movement so much that the egg is destroyed

explanation: When a tube is extra long or twisted, the muscle movements are less efficient, making it easy for the slow-moving egg to get stuck. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h2)

question: Which contraceptive option is a long-acting reversible method placed right inside the uterus?

options.A: Combined oral pill
options.B: Emergency contraceptive pill
options.C: Spermicidal foam
options.D: Intrauterine device

explanation: An IUD is a fantastic, worry-free option that sits quietly inside the uterus for years, providing continuous protection that you can stop anytime. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h3)

question: Early-onset conduct disorder in childhood is a major risk factor for which adult mental health condition?

options.A: Parkinson's disease
options.B: Alzheimer's dementia
options.C: Antisocial personality disorder
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive disorder

explanation: Severe conduct problems that begin early in life can unfortunately persist into adulthood as antisocial personality patterns if not addressed. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h7)

question: A 5-year-old child with a heavy roundworm infection has vomiting, colicky tummy pain, and a sausage-like lump felt in the belly. What is the most likely complication?

options.A: Acute glomerulonephritis
options.B: Intestinal obstruction
options.C: Hepatic abscess
options.D: Pulmonary embolism

question: Which beverage is generally allowed during the fasting period prior to the test?

options.A: Black coffee
options.B: Fruit juice
options.C: Plain water
options.D: Sweetened tea

question: A patient wants a sleep aid that doesn't cause addiction or slow down the central nervous system too much. Which option is best?

options.A: Traditional benzodiazepines
options.B: Intravenous general anesthetics
options.C: Short-acting barbiturates
options.D: Melatonin receptor agonists

explanation: Melatonin agonists mimic your body's own natural sleep hormone, which helps you avoid the heavy brain-slowdown and addiction risks of stronger pills. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h3)

question: What is the very first step in the management control process?

options.A: Taking corrective action steps
options.B: Comparing results against targets

options.D: Establishing performance standards

explanation: Before you can measure or fix anything, you need to set clear guidelines so everyone knows what good performance looks like! [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h2)

question: What does it mean if a symptom shows up long after the normal incubation window has passed?

options.A: The patient's immune system is too perfect
options.B: The disease has been totally cured by magic
options.C: The laboratory test results are always wrong
options.D: It points to a different sickness or a newer exposure

question: A postoperative patient who had surgery for a ruptured ectopic pregnancy suddenly becomes pale, dizzy, and has a dropping blood pressure. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.B: Help the patient get out of bed and walk around the room to improve circulation
options.C: Offer the patient a warm cup of tea and a light snack to boost her energy
options.D: Wait quietly for the next scheduled doctor's round in the morning

question: Which of the following is NOT a common unhealthy coping mechanism associated with high chronic stress?

options.D: Withdrawing from social and physical movement

question: What does the term 'pulse deficit' mean in clinical practice?

question: What is the main job of 'tail coverage' when using a claims-made insurance policy?

options.A: To lower the monthly premium cost for brand new graduate nurses

options.C: To pay for accidental property damage inside the hospital breakroom
options.D: To provide extra financial compensation if the nurse is injured on duty

explanation: Tail coverage acts like a safety bridge when you leave a job or retire, protecting you from late lawsuits about past shifts. [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h3)

question: A patient complains of severe stomach pain. What does a nurse with strong analytical skills do first?

options.A: Give the strongest pain medication available immediately
options.B: Discharge the patient because pain scales are unreliable
options.C: Tell the patient that stomach pain is normal after surgery
options.D: Check surgical history, lab results, and current medications

explanation: Analytical skills help the nurse look at multiple data sources to understand the root cause before acting. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h3)

question: How does boosting a patient's understanding of food directly help their health?

options.A: It cures all existing vitamin deficiencies overnight

options.C: It empowers them to make healthier food choices on their own

question: For a mother who had a safe, normal delivery, when should her very first post-natal check happen?

question: You are caring for a wound infection patient on contact precautions. What should you do before stepping out of their room?

options.D: Spray the hallway floor with a strong chlorine disinfectant

question: Why is it important to talk through the exercise steps with your patient beforehand?

question: What is the main job of descriptive statistics in nursing research?

options.C: To predict future disease outbreaks using probability
options.D: To test complex hypotheses with small sample sizes

explanation: You've got this! Descriptive statistics are simply tools to tidy up large piles of data, making it easy for us to see the main picture without getting bogged down in numbers. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do displaced persons living in crowded temporary camps often face sudden disease outbreaks?

options.A: A genetic predisposition unique to populations forced from their homes

options.C: The intentional release of biological agents within temporary settlement zones
options.D: Overcrowding combined with compromised sanitation and clean water shortages

question: Why is a nurse considered the final safety net during medication administration?

options.D: Because hospital management shifts all legal penalties solely to the nursing staff

question: Why are weekly feedback graphs posted on the staff notice board helpful?

options.A: They show nurses the tangible impact and results of their hard work
options.B: They prevent family members from visiting patients too often
options.C: They act as legal documents for the court if a patient sues
options.D: They replace the need for any verbal handovers between shifts

explanation: Seeing positive trends on a graph motivates the team to keep up their efforts and proves the new practice is working. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why does a shortened fallopian tube raise the risk of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: The fertilized egg implants inside the tube before reaching the uterus

options.C: Tubal smooth muscle completely loses its ability to contract

question: Which questionnaire is widely used to check different parts of female sexual function?

options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Beck Depression Inventory
options.D: Female Sexual Function Index

explanation: You got it! The FSFI is the go-to tool researchers and clinicians use to measure things like desire, arousal, and comfort. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h6)

question: Why must you wait for the alcohol swab on a vial stopper to air dry?

options.C: Chemicals in wet alcohol deactivate the live vaccine virus
options.D: Wet alcohol ruins the rubber stopper and causes leaks

question: A nurse says, 'I am worried this medication dose is too high for a patient with kidney disease.' Which technique is being used?

options.B: Passive avoidance
options.C: The silent treatment

question: What size syringe is standard for administering an intradermal injection?

options.A: Large gravity syringe of 10 mL
options.B: Tuberculin syringe of 1 mL
options.C: Hypodermic syringe of 3 mL
options.D: Insulin syringe of 0.5 mL

question: As a nurse, what is your top priority when assessing someone with suspected food poisoning?

options.A: Measuring chest wall expansion depth
options.B: Assessing deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Evaluating current hydration status
options.D: Testing visual acuity and eye movement

question: In pharmacology, what do we mean by the term 'pharmacokinetics'?

options.C: What the body does to a drug
options.D: How diseases destroy medication inside cells

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard type of shock seen in children?

options.B: Distributive shock
options.C: Hypovolemic shock
options.D: Metabolic shock

question: Besides a poor diet, what is another very common cause of low iron levels in older adults?

options.B: Excessive absorption of iron in the stomach
options.C: Rapid destruction of iron by liver enzymes
options.D: High levels of stomach acid locking up iron

question: How does a community nurse act as a bridge for families?

options.B: By importing expensive foreign supplements for every home
options.C: By connecting scientific guidelines with the daily realities of households
options.D: By building physical bridges across local rivers for food transport

explanation: Nurses translate complex health information into practical advice that fits what families can actually afford and access. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h2)

question: What shows that your discharge teaching for a stroke caregiver was truly effective?

options.A: Handing the family a large textbook on neurology on the day of discharge

options.C: Assuming family members already know how to operate transfer belts
options.D: Teaching care techniques in small, manageable steps with return demonstrations

explanation: Having them show you back (return demonstration) is the best way to make sure they feel confident and safe doing it at home. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T9#GNS324_U4_T9_h7)

question: What test is commonly used to check if a patient is strong enough to come off mechanical ventilation?

options.A: Arterial blood gas challenge
options.B: Continuous positive pressure test
options.C: Pulmonary function spirometry
options.D: Spontaneous breathing trial

question: What is the primary danger associated with myxedema coma?

question: What is the main goal of the 'sensitivity' part of a urine culture and sensitivity (C&S) test?

options.C: To calculate the patient's specific gravity and hydration status
options.D: To check if red blood cells are fragile under chemical stress

question: In Nigeria, why do nutrition educators often suggest combining beans and grains in a meal?

options.C: To reduce the total carbohydrate content of the pot
options.D: To provide a complete complement of essential amino acids

question: A patient with a history of stomach ulcers has joint pain. Which drug group should make you extra careful as a nurse?

options.C: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: Co-analgesic nerve medications

explanation: NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) block protective factors in the stomach lining. For a patient with ulcers, this can easily trigger bleeding! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why is collaboration with traditional birth attendants and local volunteers important for a PHC nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for government-supplied medications
options.B: It ensures that traditional workers stop practicing completely
options.C: It fosters teamwork and bridges traditional practices with formal health services
options.D: It allows the nurse to transfer all clinical responsibilities to volunteers

explanation: Collaborating with local groups helps guide traditional practices safely and encourages mothers to seek formal care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h7)

question: How did Nigerian mothers traditionally space their children before modern contraceptives arrived?

options.A: Daily ingestion of synthetic hormone pills
options.B: Intrauterine copper device insertion
options.C: Surgical tubal ligation procedures
options.D: Prolonged breastfeeding and postpartum abstinence

explanation: Traditional Nigerian societies used natural, reliable spacing methods like extended breastfeeding and resting from sex after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h5)

question: What is a key action during a nursing medication review?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop taking all prescribed treatments
options.B: Changing the hospital's drug supply company without approval
options.C: Comparing prescribed drugs against the patient's current diagnoses
options.D: Ordering new laboratory equipment from foreign manufacturers

explanation: A proper review ensures every medication matches a genuine, active medical need rather than an outdated or unverified condition. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which type of heart tumour do nurses see more often in clinical practice?

options.A: Primary papillary fibroelastomas
options.B: Primary malignant sarcomas
options.C: Congenital rhabdomyomas
options.D: Secondary metastatic tumours

explanation: Cancers that travel to the heart from other parts of the body (metastatic tumours) actually happen much more often than tumours that start directly in the heart tissue. Everyday nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which physical sign is a classic telltale clue of an opioid overdose?

options.A: Excessive sweating
options.B: High fever
options.C: Pinpoint pupils
options.D: Wide dilated pupils

explanation: Spotting tiny, constricted pupils (miosis) is one of the classic physical signs that instantly helps nurses suspect an opioid overdose in the ward. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h4)

question: A newly diagnosed patient tells you, 'The lab results are mixed up; I feel fine!' Which stage of grief is this?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Denial
options.C: Bargaining
options.D: Anger

explanation: Spot on! Refusing to believe a scary diagnosis is a classic way patients protect themselves from sudden emotional shock. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T5#GNS221_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which sign tells you a patient has severe malaria instead of just uncomplicated malaria?

options.A: Impaired consciousness or coma
options.B: Loss of appetite
options.C: Mild intermittent headache
options.D: Low-grade joint pain

explanation: Spot on! Any sign of confusion, extreme weakness, or coma (cerebral malaria) means it's an emergency needing immediate inpatient care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why do complication rates from unsafe abortions tend to be higher in villages than in cities?

options.A: Delays in reaching qualified medical help worsen emergency outcomes
options.B: Rural women have better access to sterile surgical instruments
options.C: Traditional healers in villages always use modern antibiotics
options.D: Rural clinics are strictly reserved for reproductive emergencies

explanation: You nailed it. Long travel times mean infections and bleeding go unchecked for too long before reaching a nurse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: Which enzyme helps HIV convert its viral RNA into DNA inside the host cell?

options.A: Reverse transcriptase
options.B: Amylase
options.C: Pepsin
options.D: DNA polymerase

explanation: HIV uses an enzyme called reverse transcriptase to rewrite its genetic code from RNA into DNA so it can hide inside our body's cells. Clever little virus, but now you know its trick! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h2)

question: What blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the placenta back to the fetus?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Spiral endometrial artery
options.D: Umbilical artery

explanation: The umbilical vein is responsible for carrying freshly oxygenated and nutrient-rich blood from the placental villi back to the fetal circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h1)

question: What protein makes up the thick filaments in a sarcomere?

options.A: Tropomyosin
options.B: Myosin
options.C: Actin
options.D: Troponin

explanation: Thick filaments are composed of the protein myosin, which features small heads that pull on thin actin filaments. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Long-term exposure to environmental toxins
options.B: Severe bacterial infections in early childhood
options.C: Faulty genes passed down from parents
options.D: Nutritional deficiencies during pregnancy

explanation: These conditions stem from genetic mutations inherited through family bloodlines rather than external lifestyle factors. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h1)

question: What do we mean when we talk about a patient's 'health literacy'?

options.A: The capacity to process and understand basic health information
options.B: The speed at which a patient can swallow multiple tablets
options.C: The total number of years a patient spent in formal education
options.D: The ability to read advanced medical textbooks and journals

explanation: Health literacy is simply how well someone can understand basic health info to make good choices about their body and care. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h1)

question: A patient stumbles when walking and cannot coordinate their finger-to-nose movement during a physical exam. Which brain structure is most likely impaired?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: Inability to perform smooth coordinated movements or maintain balance points directly to cerebellar dysfunction. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h5)

question: What natural biological feature in adolescent females makes them more vulnerable to certain sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Cervical ectopy
options.B: Enlarged ovarian follicles
options.C: Thickened endometrial lining
options.D: Hyperactive uterine peristalsis

explanation: You nailed it! Cervical ectopy exposes more delicate cells on the outer cervix, making young women biologically more susceptible to infections. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why are patients receiving strong antibiotic therapy at higher risk for developing oral fungal infections?

options.A: Antibiotics kill normal protective bacteria, allowing fungi to overgrow.
options.B: Antibiotics harden the tooth enamel and trap food particles in the gums.
options.C: Antibiotics directly stimulate the taste buds to produce excess sugar.
options.D: Antibiotics immediately inflame the hard palate and block saliva ducts.

explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics wipe out the harmless resident bacteria that normally keep fungal populations in check within the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h7)
